local.title: Big lawns on **heavy ground.**
local.intro: Lawns in Mundy Township come in two sizes: subdivision lots on sewer, and the acre or more the zoning asks for where there is no sewer. Both usually sit on heavy soil that drains slowly. A good weekly cut here comes down to keeping up in May and staying off the soft spots.

points.title: Acre lots, long passes
points.body: On a lot of an acre or more, a zero turn and a straight pattern cover the ground cleanly, and the stripes run long. We match the pattern to the yard: straight on open ground, curved around the drive and the cul-de-sac.

points.title: Keeping up with spring
points.body: MSU Extension says to remove no more than a third of the blade at a time, and that fast spring growth can call for a cut every four to five days. A big lawn that misses a week in May shows it for a month.

points.title: Wet ground, careful turns
points.body: Much of the township's heavy soil stays wet after rain. Turning a riding mower on saturated soil can pack it and tear the turf, MSU Extension warns, so on wet weeks our turns go wider and the low corners wait until the end.

points.title: Younger lawns, higher deck
points.body: About a quarter of the homes here went up in 2000 or later, and their lawns are still young. MSU Extension says a higher cut keeps grass more stress tolerant in summer heat and shades out crabgrass, so we run the deck high.

logistics.title: Setting up weekly mowing in Mundy Township.
body: Rob prices the season after walking the lawn with you, and from then on you have a set mowing day. The crew arrives on it each week with zero turns, trimmers and blowers on the trailer.

A visit runs in the same order every time: mow, trim around the house, beds, trees, mailbox post and fences, edge the walks and drive, and blow the hard surfaces clean. Clippings stay on the lawn, as MSU Extension recommends, since they break down quickly and return nutrients.
Pair the season with a [spring cleanup](/spring-cleanup-mundy-township-mi/) and [leaf removal](/leaf-removal-mundy-township-mi/), and the lawn is handled from the first cut to the last.

faq.q: Do you mow lawns in Mundy Township?
faq.a: Yes. Grand Scapes mows residential lawns in Mundy Township every week on a set day, from subdivision lots to acre parcels. Every visit is a full mow, trim and edge, with the walks and drive blown clean. The estimate is free.

faq.q: Do you mow large lots and acreage?
faq.a: Yes. We have kept a 7 1/2 acre lawn for a full season, so an acre lot is ordinary work for us, and acre lots are common in the township wherever homes are not on sewer. Bigger lots take more time, so each one is priced after Rob sees it.

faq.q: How often should my lawn be mowed in Michigan?
faq.a: Weekly covers most of the season. MSU Extension's rule is to cut no more than a third of the blade at once, which in fast spring growth can mean every four to five days. Summer slows down, and the deck stays high in the heat.

faq.q: Can you mow when the ground is wet?
faq.a: Sometimes, and carefully. Much of Mundy Township is slow draining heavy soil, and MSU Extension warns that turning mowers on saturated soil packs it and damages turf. On a soaked day we change the turns, skip the low spots or move the visit.
